Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From f75c9f110f0bc2cba401a8b95c9c4377c6c057e9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eran Mizrahi <eranmizra@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2011 21:10:37 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

This fixes a problem introduced by commit 43e45eb94e1
which (wrongly) handled the 0xFEFF mark as RTL.

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766

diff --git a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
index 88f72594567..54bb57f0a80 100644
--- a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
+++ b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
@@ -1692,7 +1692,7 @@ public class TextUtils {
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }
 
     /**
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `TextUtils.java`**
   - A single line of code was modified in the `TextUtils` class. The condition that checks for a range of Unicode characters was changed from:
     ```java
     (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)
     ```
     to:
     ```java
     (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)
     ```
   - This change effectively excludes the Unicode character 0xFEFF from being treated as part of the RTL (Right-to-Left) character range.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `TextUtils.java` addresses a bug that was introduced by a previous commit (identified as 43e45eb94e1). The earlier implementation incorrectly classified the special Unicode marker 0xFEFF as an RTL character. The current patch corrects this by adjusting the upper limit of the character range check, ensuring that 0xFEFF is no longer included in the RTL handling logic. This change is crucial for proper text rendering and handling of Unicode characters in applications that rely on this functionality.

2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the Unicode character 0xFEFF, which is a special marker known as the Zero Width No-Break Space (ZWNBSP). In the previous implementation, this character was mistakenly included in the range of RTL characters, leading to improper text rendering and handling in applications that utilize this functionality. The fix involved adjusting the character range to exclude 0xFEFF, ensuring that it is not treated as an RTL character.
